items.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: guys like Hal Blaine, the drummer from the Wrecking Crew and those people, they had so many sessions.

ctx.x: Some of the guys were even telling me that if they had to go out of town they tried not to let people know because as a session musician if your phone rings and you don’t pick ups then —

Yeah. Well it was so busy back then, everybody had an answering service. And after every session, everybody’d be out in the hall on the — not cell phones — on the pay phones, calling their service to see what dates were booked for them the next day or the next week or that type of thing. And they’d be writing in their book. And that’s where Cartage Company started up in LA because guys like Hal Blaine, the drummer from the Wrecking Crew and those people, they had so many sessions. They may do a 10:00 session for…
at 2:00 he’d be at United Western Studio with his other drum set already set up. And maybe at 6:00 it’d be the third studio with his third drum set. That’s the way it was.
